To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
vaccination induces an accelerated interferon gamma response by CD4(+) T cells in the lungs during subsequent Mycobacterium Tuberculosis (Mtb) infection.
vaccination with Mtb induces IL 23 dependent IL 17 production that is important in establishing a protective immune response against Mtb.

IL 17 is essential for establishment of an accelerated interferon gamma producing T cell population in lung tissue after vaccination with a subunit vaccine and subsequent challenge with Mycobacterium Tuberculosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of IL 17 in pulmonary CD4+ responses to Mycobacterium bovis BCG vaccination and M. tuberculosis challenge.
the mechanisms that underlie protective CD4+ T helper cell responses to mycobacterial infection, and how these responses are affected by vaccination.
the development of a new vaccine against tuberculosis (TB).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL 17 is a key cytokine that drives the recruitment of protective CD4+ T effector cells to the lung during M. tuberculosis infection, thereby restricting the bacterial growth.

the vaccination of mice against M. tuberculosis with a recombinant BCG vaccine, which is based on a plasmid expressing the antigen 85B of Mycobacterium, triggers an accelerated recall response by CD4 T cells producing interferons in the lung during M. tuberculosis infection, and this response is mediated by IL 17 producing cells that are induced during vaccination.
IL 17 is essential for the recruitment of IFN-g+ T cells in response to M. tuberculosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

vaccination induces a population of IL-17 producing CD4 T cells that are recruited to the lung during challenge, where they induce the production of CXCL9, 10, and 11, which in turn recruits interferon g producing CD4 T cell that limit bacterial growth.
vaccination induces a CD4+ T-cell response that is protective during Mycobacterum tuberculosis challenge.
IL-17 producing CD4 T cells are important for the early control of M. tuberculosis infection and that this response is dependent on IL-23.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the vaccine can induce the production of a population of IL-17 producing CD4 T cells that, upon infection, can trigger the production of CXCL9,10,11 that recruit interferon g producing CD4 T-cells to the lung, which can restrict the growth of the pathogen.
the IL 23-IL 17 axis is important for the early establishment and maintenance of a CD4 T cell response in the lung after vaccination and subsequent challenge.

the vaccine induced IL 17 producing T cell population is important for the recruitment of CD4+ interferon g producing cells to the lung, and that the vaccine induced population is important for controlling M. tuberculosis infection
